meta.note: Prices verified against provider documentation on the date above. Provider pricing changes; the figure that matters is your own measured cost per conversation. Treat this as a planning model, not an invoice.

caveats.title: Newer models can cost more per word at the same price per token
caveats.body: Claude Opus 4.7 and later use a newer tokenizer that produces roughly 30% more tokens for the same text than Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier. A model with an identical headline price can therefore cost about 30% more for identical input. Cost models that compare only $/MTok miss this entirely.

caveats.title: Claude Sonnet 5 introductory pricing ends 31 August 2026
caveats.body: Sonnet 5 is $2/$10 per MTok through 31 August 2026, then $3/$15 — a 50% increase. If your forecast assumes current pricing beyond that date, it is roughly 50% light on that line item.

caveats.title: Cache writes cost more than ordinary input
caveats.body: A 5-minute cache write is 1.25x base input price and a 1-hour write is 2x. A cache read is 0.1x. Caching only pays off once content is actually re-read — after one read for the 5-minute tier, two for the 1-hour tier. Caching a prompt that is never reused makes it more expensive, not less.

caveats.title: Tool definitions are billed on every single call
caveats.body: Tool schemas sit in the input of every request, plus a per-model tool-use system prompt of roughly 286–804 tokens. An agent with fifteen verbose tool definitions pays for all fifteen on every turn, whether it calls them or not — one of the most common invisible costs in agent systems.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.notes: Strong default for classification, extraction and routing sub-tasks.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.notes: Highest tier. Rarely the right default for high-volume agent traffic.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.notes: Cheapest credible option here — useful as the low end of a routing tier.

models.name: GPT-5 Nano
models.notes: Viable for narrow classification and routing where quality is measurable.

presets.name: Customer support agent
presets.description: Multi-turn support conversations with retrieval over a help centre and two or three tools.

presets.name: Internal knowledge assistant
presets.description: Employee-facing RAG assistant over internal documents. Long retrieved context, short answers.

presets.name: Multi-agent research workflow
presets.description: Orchestrator plus specialised sub-agents. The pattern where costs most often surprise teams — every sub-agent turn is a billed call.

presets.name: Document extraction pipeline
presets.description: High-volume structured extraction. Batch-friendly and the clearest case for a cheap model.

presets.name: Coding agent
presets.description: Long-horizon sessions with large file context and heavy tool use. Token-hungry by nature.
